At it's best and most immersive, Chivalry 2 is two teams of thirty-two players participating in deep and immersive combat with an incredibly high skill ceiling and filled to the brim with emergent strategy. Words of aggressive faction loyalty fill the chat and the clash of steel and screams of soldiers fighting for their lives fill your ears. 

At it's most degenerate, Chivalry 2 is two teams of thirty-two Glenn Quagmire soundalikes screaming at the top of their lungs as they beat the opposing team to death with projectile pigs and beehives while the chat is filled with heated debate over which Tony Hawk Pro Skater game is the greatest and most memorable. All of this while completely ignoring the objective. And honestly? I love every second of it. I fully recommend this title.

Great game, not so great developers. I liked this game so much I bought it again and started playing it here on Steam (I have ~600 hours on the Epic games store version, which was released like a year before the steam release). They also talked about letting us transfer progress when it was finally released on steam (but didn't, and never talked about it again, a theme veteran players are all too familiar with)

Torn Banner really fumbled the bag on this one and lost so much potential in this game. Best thing they could do now is permanently drop the price, allow private servers, and let the modding community take over. Mods will create new life in this dead boi, Helm's Deep with Chivalry 2 combat, imagine! Ranked servers, new player friendly servers, etc. 

As of now the new player experience* is to skip the tutorial and join 64 player team objective (against players with 100s-1000s of hours played) where you go 2-20 KD every game for a few hours then uninstall. I love this game, and I hate seeing players have such a terrible experience and quit without fully unlocking the potential to have fun, because once you have full control over your game, the opportunities to have fun are endless. But I also know a lot of OG players who have quit (and I miss them, dearly).
This game is a sandbox for creativity and fun, all the templates are there, the mechanics are there, it just needs to have it's gate open by the devs. Give us private servers and mod support and you'll see a second wind in this gem whose potential is being stunted. 

*Perfect example is this free to play weekend (12/9/23), every time it's on sale or free to play - dormant toxic level 800-1000s come back and stomp the new players. I only see these mediocre players come back when it's a free weekend or something happened where there's an influx of new players. Really sad to see, because they gatekeep the hell out of the new player experience.

First of all, the Atmosphere in the game is great, the combat system feels nice and takes a while to get used to. Maps are gorgeous and littered with small titbits and pieces causing a really cool sim-like world. Archers, Catapults, Trebuchets, Siege towers, ballistae, ... It's simply cool and the voice acting and emotes are top-notch (aside from the one announcer not knowing how to pronounce Trebuchet).

Throw a fish from a well at someone, steal the pigs and peasants to bring to your ship, topple a stone monument, light a library on fire, kill a Duke, ... The game generally is gorgeous and fun and incredibly fun when you have a balanced match.

*BUT*, there's THE issue.

The reason I'm not recommending it is simple, at the start of every game you have numerous high skilled players swapping to the Attacking side leading to a MASSIVE imbalance. This, combined with various people who are AFK on the defensive side, just leads to a slaughter. You spawn, end up being 3v1'd near instantly without much of a chance to react, rinse and repeat seal-clubbing until the map ends.

Sometimes a match not even lasts 6 minutes from start to finish, everyone on the defensive side simply gets crushed to a pulp, people on the attacking team with their imbalanced numbers hardly ever die in the mass of bodies just charging forwards.

There is an autobalancing option, though it doesn't seem to work. People get forced over, they either quit or someone else swaps back over to repeat the cycle. I've seen imbalances of 39 players vs 30. That is massive and incredibly unfun.

No remarks on Dueling or FFA servers, those are genuinely pretty decent from the little I played, although I did get this game for the larger sieges and battles, hence the non-recommendation.

The negative reviews about this being a steamroll simulator are true. If you're looking for a fair, competitive experience where a skilled player can carry and turn the tide, this isn't it.

I figured out very quickly that Chivalry 2 was unfair, unbalanced, unconcerned with status, and unconcerned with whether individual skill is given room to change the outcome of a battle. Players can freely swap teams to get out of a losing situation and start kicking their old team in the teeth. If you find yourself in a 1v1 and hold your own for a bit, the enemy will ignore everyone else on your team to single out the distracted guy fending off his death, and jam a free spear into his undefended, unbaptized bits. Sometimes a catapult just obliterates you for 2550 damage with no hope of counterplay.

This is a big dumb meatgrinder where you beat other players bloody with swords and hammers, to unlock more swords and hammers. You run in and die, repeat, and every bit of the game's design acknowledges that it's meant to be this way. You even respawn freely at a full sprint and are equipped with loud, hammy, extremely-committed battle cries.

And you know what? I could cry tears of f-cking joy that they still make multiplayer games like this. It doesn't care about being esport material where celebrity-hopefuls have a ladder to climb, or whether it's watchable on stream. 

It's betting every dollar it has on the idea that if it hands you a warhammer and lets you flatten Brave Ser XxKushSniper69xX like a soda can, then you, the player, will be having carefree, selfish fun... and then it gives you 31 other knights to try and clobber, because that's 31x as much fun. Yeah, it's messy, but I have so much fun just trying to bonk the guy in front of me that I don't care at all who wins, I'm just glad to have fresh skulls to crush.

Yes, you'll almost always see one team losing badly to the other, even on something as unstructured as an open-ground team TDM battle. It's okay to be bothered by this, but personally I don't mind this even when it's my turn in the washing machine full of knives. I find this adds drama and a personal element to these matches, where it's much more satisfying to send a plate helmet clattering across the floor when it belonged to a complacent knight that thought everyone on my team would go down so easily... 

...this goes doubly for when you corner one of those much-hated archers, where they'll either win back some small dignity by putting up a decent scrap with their backup weapon, or die shamefully with a bow in their hands and piss in their grieves. There's just something about swinging a cannonball of a mace into to an enemy that's EARNED your wrath.

A couple more quick pros: as implied earlier, there's a progression/unlock system to offer you more options as you play, and the melee system is great, even if it translates kinda predictably over the net. Maps are ASTONISHINGLY gorgeous with some of the most beautiful mosques and churches I've seen in a game, and they rotate quickly without much downtime; everything about this game is constantly pushing you back into the fight for another reckless charge.

Overall, 10/10 for dumb multiplayer fun. I wish more online games were confident enough to implement a fun, simple concept and be content to let the damn thing breathe.

[h1]A hardcore yet entertaining massively multiplayer medieval hack-and-slash game with completely no chivalry at all[/h1]

[h2]8/10[/h2]

[h3]Opening[/h3]

On July 30, 2024, as the developer announced that the game would stop substantive content updates, Chivalry 2, a game released in June 2021, officially ushered in the final stage of its life. Even though the game had encountered a storm of negative reviews, this news still caused an uproar and widespread dissatisfaction among its players. Perhaps this means many players still have hope for it deep in their hearts. As of today, Chivalry 2 still has an extremely stable player number of around one thousand to two thousand, which is enough to support its survival. Rather than recreating the pure hardcore medieval hack and slash, Chivalry 2 is committed to bringing fun to players through disorder, chaos, sneak attacks, gang fights, and other despicable means and brawls without any chivalry. The many ridiculous and hilarious scenes in the game will surely leave a deep impression on you.

[h3]Strength[/h3]

Compared to its predecessor, Chivalry: Medieval Warfare, Chivalry 2 can switch freely between first-person and third-person. The operation design is easier to learn but hard to master. Unlike similar hack-and-slash games such as For Honor and Kingdom Come: Deliverance, which have a more competitive parrying system, in Chivalry 2, players only need to consume stamina to block most attacks, but this does not mean that the battles in the game lose their spectacle and strategic depth. Simply defending or attacking blindly will quickly consume all your stamina, eventually exposing your weakness and leaving you vulnerable to attack. How to calmly respond and accurately control your stamina in a chaotic and tense situation is not only the key to victory but also an important watershed to test the skills of different players. The most vulnerable archers in the game will not be killed by one blow even when they are at full health, which also provides a certain fault tolerance limit for players' operations in a relatively hardcore game environment.

The map scenes in Chivalry 2 vary greatly, from forests deserts, and fortresses, to villages islands, ice fields, and arenas. The different environmental features, map mechanisms, and mission objectives can bring players a strong sense of freshness and fun. Fixed weapons such as catapults and ballista are extremely destructive, but the existence of friendly fire also requires their operators to think twice before acting. The game excels in creating and rendering the battlefield atmosphere, with shocking scene changes and destruction effects when advancing the progress, huge crowds of people and hearty fighting, sword collisions, cheering shouts, and other excellent sound effects, and passionate music at the climax of the game. Combined with the game's realistic and bloody performances of severed limbs, it can bring players a grand, cruel yet immersive medieval battlefield experience. Chivalry 2 is also equipped with a complete robot system, allowing players to enjoy the full gaming experience in single-player mode.

[h3]Weakness[/h3]

The experience that Chivalry 2 brings to players in terms of server and game optimization can be described as disastrous. In a game that can accommodate up to 64 people and emphasizes close combat and large-scale melee, players with medium and low configurations will feel obvious lag and frame drops when the number of people increases, seriously affecting the gaming experience.  The game was repeatedly attacked by DDOS in the first half of 2024, It was extremely difficult to play a normal game at that time. The situation has only improved in recent times, In addition, the game's until-cheating system is ineffective, and cheaters are able to hide their identities in various games and get away with it. The game's localization work is even more perfunctory, with many languages being machine-translated and the meaning being extremely inaccurate.

The game's matching itself has the problem of homogeneity, making it hard to bring lasting freshness to players. The game's balance mechanism is even worse, polarized matches are the norm, and there is almost no punishment for players who quit midway. Since the attacking side has a relatively fixed and unified birth point and mission objectives, they often stick together, which can easily lead to a multi-person gang fight, the overall combat experience is relatively better; On the contrary, the game has no overtime and many terrains are easy to defend and difficult attack, which are more favorable to the defender. In addition, many offensive players generally pay more attention to their own gaming experience rather than advancing the mission objectives, making it easier for the defender to win the game when both sides are evenly matched. Weapons with long attack ranges, such as spears and lances, have a greater advantage in close combat, whereas long-range weapons such as bows and crossbows can drive players crazy. Designs that add interest, such as friendly damage and friendly collision volume, will indeed affect player operations to a certain extent.

[h3]Conclusion[/h3]

At a time when multiplayer medieval cold weapon hack-and-slash games are already scarce, Chivalry 2, which focuses on multiplayer gaming experience, is destined to have incomparable advantages over games like Mount & Blade and Kingdom Come: Deliverance; compared with MORDHAU, it is much easier to get started. The chaotic, hardcore, yet fun and entertaining gaming experience makes Chivalry 2 a leader in this field. It is true that the game has many problems in optimization, server, until-cheating, and balance, but Chivalry 2 is still able to stand strong due to the lack of alternatives.

Chivalry 2 is certainly worth a try and could bring you a lot of fun, but don't forget that it is still a difficult game to master. Players may need to think twice about whether it is worth investing time in a game that has stopped updating content. In a game environment filled with veterans and masters, it may be very difficult for Chivalry 2 to absorb more fresh blood. All aspects may reveal that Chivalry 2 is a game that is extremely selective in its audience.

Long version:
The controls are almost exactly the same to Mordhau.

Now what I didn't realize at first, and felt like the game was "unresponsive", is that your mouse movement DOES NOT control the direction of your swing. Surely you can move your hips to accelerate or delay your swings, but by purely pressing M1 you will always initiate a swing attack from the right, and your second M1 swing will always come from the left. You can only change your first swing by holding the ALT key while pressing M1, to initiate the swing from the left.
But what possibly makes up for it, is your ability to charge your attacks into a heavy attack. These attacks come with a significant delay for increased damage, which additionally to your hip movement, add a layer of variety that Mordhau does not have.
Much like in Mordhau, you can combo and feint all types of attacks into a different one.
I also really appreciate that a block can be held, no matter the weapon. Your block has its own "stamina", which can either be broken with consecutive attacks, or a kick. Besides, shields can be damaged and even completely destroyed, which gives a lot more leverage against turtles.
In Mordhau, you would find that dodging is bound to a perk. But in Chivalry any class can dodge.
The chambers you would know from Mordhau are different in Chivalry. In Chivalry, "Chambers" (called "Counters") are initiated by blocking, before you hit them with the same attack that they are winding up. So Chambers happen less on accident, and must be thoughtfully prepared.
Now, unique to Chivalry 2, they have introduced "Jabs". Jabs are like quick punches, which can be used to cancel an enemies attack during their windup. They add an element of variety that I wished Mordhau could use as well.
Every weapon comes with a so called "special attack", which is an attack simply executed by a single press of that assigned key. Special attacks deal more damage. For example, the special attack of the Longsword is the infamous "Mordhau". The attack can not be used in a combo. I guess they tried, but it feels very lackluster compared to the Alternative Grip of Mordhau, which can be used at will.
Throwing weapons feels weird in Chivalry. I feel very confident in my throwing abilities in Mordhau, where the items you throw have a certain weight and feel to them. But for Chivalry I'm not even sure if they use a proper physics engine for the projectiles. They feel like whatever you throw is on a destined pre-calculated path. And with that weird foggy trail it draws, you can barely see if you were close to hitting your target or not. It's very hard to tell the distance/time your projectile has travelled. Which, I do remember, is the same issue I had with Chivalry 1.


I find that the exchange of hits, blocks and counters is a lot more fluid compared to Mordhau. On the other hand, combat also feels much less precise and hitboxes seem to be a lot larger.
It makes sense, considering that armor is of cosmetic nature. You have less reason to aim for specific body parts, with the exception of heads.

After almost 3000 hours in Mordhau, I decided to give Chivalry 2 a try when it was on sale (I recommend buying it when it’s 80–90% off).

The first big difference is clear: the entry barrier is much more accessible.

The combat system allows you to hold block, which makes mistakes less punishing and helps new players survive longer in fights. Also, parry and chamber are more forgiving, even giving a bit of a “invulnerability”, which makes fighting multiple enemies easier.

This doesn’t mean the game is simple. A skilled player will still outperform a new one without any problem.

If you come from Mordhau or Chivalry 1, you will notice some important changes:
- Drags and accels are not as important as before (but still useful).
- Combat feels more forgiving and less punishing for certain mistakes.
- Feinting with Q is no longer the easy way to kill another player.

If you come from Mount & Blade or similar games, the change is even bigger, since there is no directional blocking system here.

The maps and the feeling of being in a medieval battle are one of its strongest points. They did a good job here. Maps are fun and you can clearly see the fight between two fronts.

I’ve seen many reviews talking about hackers or cheaters. In my 50 hours so far, I haven’t seen any, just good players. About toxicity, it’s nothing unusual, just the typical behavior you see in any PvP game.

If you like medieval combat games and enjoyed titles like Chivalry 1, Mordhau or Mount & Blade, you will probably like this game. That said, as I mentioned before, I recommend waiting for a sale.

This lag is not reflective on individual players pings and is instead coming from the Torn Banner servers directly. 

Whether Torn Banner knows of these issues or are simply ignoring them is unknown, as the developers have effectively abandoned the game at this point. There is a vague "Path Forward" the developers put out several months ago which the developers claimed that the game is "feature complete". This statement being made while a plethora of bugs still plague the game, many of which have been present since or around launch. 

The disappointing fact is that at this point, an otherwise enjoyable game is not worth purchasing or playing because it is nearly unplayable with certain connection issues and bugs. You have been warned - perhaps pick up the game once you've gotten some measure of assurance that the game will receive better support in the future, if that is even possible now with the Torn Banner moving on to a new IP entirely.

Broken mechanics/Bugs:
1) Forced Repost - Occurs when a counter is inputted and a counter window visually appears open, but you initiate a repost 
2) Forced Repost Counter feint - Occurs when a counter and counter feint is inputted and a counter window visually appears open, but you initiate a repost 
3) Red Counter  - Occurs when a counter is inputted and a counter window visually appears open, but you take damage from your opponent's attack instead of receiving the counter
4) Red Counter feint - Occurs when a counter and counter feint is inputted and a counter window visually appears open, but you take damage from your opponent's attack instead of receiving the counter

[h1] My Personal Favorite - Chivalry II [/h1]

After playing many hours of Chiv on my Epic Games account [~800 hrs. / LVL 400+] I purchased the game on Steam. After accumulating these many hours, I can confirm [b]this is one of the best games on the internet.[/b] While the game is far from perfect, as many other users have touched on in other reviews, Torn Banner is actively working to improve the gaming experience. 

[hr][/hr]

Much of the combat is centered around making you feel like the main character of a true medieval battle with all the violence, blood, and silliness along the way. Stab your best friend with a long sword, chop the archer's head off who shot you in the back, physically THROW yourself into the fray with the catapult, or even find a bench and start drinking with the enemy! The possibilities are endless.

Although the tutorial is crucial in understanding the basics, the game's mechanics are easy enough to pick up. If you're brand new to this type of fighting game, you may initially find it difficult to perform some of the more advanced maneuvers. With a little practice (and maybe some luck!), you'll be spinning around like a Beyblade in no time! The game rewards practice and patience, so don't be discouraged if you're not as practiced as the guy across the field. 

The game's skill cap is extremely high. Even as a seasoned veteran of the game, I still find duelists and players that wipe the floor with me. The nice thing is many of these high-level players are also more than happy to explain how they just kicked your booty and will help you improve.

[hr][/hr]

Some common complaints about many games within the genre are that it harbors Nazis and other toxic and hateful individuals. Torn Banner has put their foot down and has been actively muting and banning those who are reported spewing hate speech and other slurs that degrade the importance of the game - killing the other guys. This is the game for you if you're looking for a low-toxic game. If you're a Nazi or otherwise hurtful/toxic individual, [u]we don't want you here.[/u]

Another common complaint is hacking. I have only seen one person 'hacking', but it was truly a client-side glitch that made only his head and sword visible (everything else was invisible). So I guess I'm trying to say if you think someone killed you with a hack, it was most likely someone more seasoned at the game.

[hr][/hr]
